newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas firms in Alberta, falls in East.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas firms in Alberta, falls in East.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for Wednesday delivery were higher in Alberta but sharply lower at the Niagara and Sumas export points, industry sources said Tuesday.
At the AECO storage hub, prices gained about two cents to about C$1.45 per gigajoule (GJ) despite forecasts for a continuance of mild weather in Calgary through the weekend.
Sources attributed the uptick to heating demand in Manitoba and a mild correction following a week of softening.
These prices are still about 80 cents lower than week-ago levels.
Lifted by the firmer daily market, March AECO prices climbed into the C$1.52-1.54 per GJ range, sources said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices lost another 10-14 cents to the $1.33-1.38 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area, as Northwest restored most service on its system.
The pipeline company said it returned to service its 26-inch mainline in western Washington, except for a 15-mile section near Yelm.
This section of the pipeline, which was isolated when land movement was detected on Vail Mountain, will not be returned to service until ground work is complete, the company said.
However, there has been no disruption in gas service, the company added.
At Niagara, prices fell more than 30 cents to about $2.09 per mmBtu as temperatures rose in eastern Canada and storage supplies were ample.
